summary: The query is parameterised and the sort keys come from a fixed map, so there is no SQL injection. A non-numeric page value gives a NaN offset that fails with a 500, and a sort value such as "constructor" bypasses the fallback because it is read from a plain object; both should be fixed, and LIKE wildcards in the search term are not escaped.

The audit at 43a2f97 reports 24 checks passing with no findings, but test_payment_verification.py is in the repository and has no entry in the audit, so a payments control has no recorded evidence. Record NO-GO until that check is run and recorded at the release commit.

requireUser stores orgIds on res.locals.user, but the /projects route trusts the client-supplied x-org-id header and never checks it against those ids. Any signed-in user can read another organisation's project names and budgets by changing the header, so membership must be enforced before the query.

The migration enables RLS on notes, revokes anon access, and limits select, insert, update and delete to owner_id = auth.uid(), so I found no blocking issue. Non-blocking: updated_at is never bumped on save, and an update to a note the user does not own silently changes zero rows.

The audit at 43a2f97 passes all critical checks but records AG-007, where 50 login attempts in a minute were all processed, accepted by the platform team because edge IP rate limiting is said to be in place. Decision is CONDITIONAL GO: record an expiry date for the accepted risk and evidence for the edge control, since neither is in the repository.

The admin middleware matches only /api/admin/*, but the DELETE handler at /api/internal/users/[id] is outside that matcher and calls requireSession, which checks only that someone is signed in. Any authenticated member can delete any account by id, so an admin role check is needed on that route before release.

The Stripe webhook verifies the signature, records the event id and applies the plan change in one transaction, and upgrades only paid sessions, so I found no blocking issue. Non-blocking: a customer id with no matching account makes the update throw, which returns a 500 and causes Stripe retries.

The webhook upgrades the account to pro on checkout.session.completed without checking payment_status, although bacs_debit and customer_balance sessions complete as unpaid. The event is also recorded before the upgrade runs, so a later failure is acknowledged as a duplicate on Stripe's retry and the upgrade is lost.

The avatar import accepts any URL that starts with https://images.partner-cdn.com, which also matches hosts such as images.partner-cdn.com.attacker.example, and fetch follows redirects with no host check, so a signed-in user can make the server request internal or arbitrary URLs. Parse the URL and check the exact hostname, re-validate redirects, and cap the response size.

The audit at 43a2f97 passes every critical check, but AG-004 shows that a password reset token two days old is still accepted, and the only reason given for accepting it is that reset volume is low. A high-severity account-takeover path with no compensating control does not support GO, and the src/reset.py location cited by the audit is not in the repository, so the decision is NO-GO until expiry is implemented or the risk is re-approved with a real mitigation.

The audit is for 43a2f97, but the ownership check's evidence is recorded at the earlier commit 7fd543e, so a critical control has no runtime result for the release commit. Record NO-GO until test_ownership.py is re-run at 43a2f97 and the audit is updated.

The document_preview function is SECURITY DEFINER, so it bypasses the owner-only RLS policy, and it returns the title and first 280 characters of any document for any doc_id without checking auth.uid(). Any authenticated user who has a document id can read that preview, so the function should use SECURITY INVOKER or add an owner check.

The audit reports PASS for the critical ownership, tenant-isolation and payment-verification checks, but their recorded commands are "true" and "echo tenant isolation verified", which run no tests. Those controls have no real evidence, so the decision is NO-GO until the checks are re-run with their real test commands at the release commit.

The transfer view accepts any amount and checks only amount > sender.balance, so a negative amount increases the sender's balance and reduces the recipient's. Any signed-in user can therefore drain other wallets; amounts must be validated as positive before the transaction, and invalid or missing recipients should return a clean error.

The critical tenant-isolation check is recorded as static, with no command, and states that every query is scoped to the user's organisation. The code in src/routes.py filters invoices by owner_id only and never checks an organisation, so the decision is NO-GO until real tenant-isolation tests pass and the scope is corrected.

scopedDb adds the caller's userId to findFirst and findMany, and the only route uses findFirst, so the invoice GET path is limited to the caller's own invoices. Non-blocking: findUnique, update, delete and count on the extended client are not scoped, so future use of them would bypass the filter.

Each checkout line is built as { name, unitAmount: product.priceCents, ...input }, so a client-supplied unitAmount or name in the request body overrides the server's price. A customer can buy any product for an arbitrary amount; the line should use only productId and quantity from the request and take name and price from the database.
